content: Plain JSON.parse/JSON.stringify round-tripping destroys comments, key order, whitespace, and trailing commas. Libraries like comment-json, node-jsonc-parser (jsonc-parser, used by VS Code), and doctor-json perform format-preserving surgical edits so only the changed value differs in output; everything else stays byte-identical. GSD's config.json is plain JSON (not JSONC) so comments aren't the primary risk, but unknown/future keys and key ordering are — a naive parse-mutate-stringify cycle silently drops keys the schema doesn't know about unless the tool explicitly round-trips the full parsed object rather than reconstructing it from the schema.
